########## d65522e ##########
feat(bk7258): chain outbound Wi-Fi frames into one mailbox transaction

wifi_transmit() handed the CP one frame per mailbox transaction, and when
the link was already busy it returned -EBUSY and the frame was dropped.
The CP has always been able to walk a chain -- cif_main.c:94 iterates
"for (i = 0; i < msg.num && head != NULL; i++)" -- and the vendor's own AP
firmware exploits that in wdrv_txdata_pre_process() (bk_avdk_smp AP,
components/bk_wifi_driver/wdrv_tx.c:182): frames accumulate while a batch
is outstanding, a sending_flag suppresses re-entry, and tx completion
kicks the next batch.  On failure the vendor keeps the frame rather than
freeing it.

Mirror that.  Pending frames go on a private index chain (chain_next,
sentinel WIFI_TX_CHAIN_END) instead of the shared cpdu chain, because the
CP rewrites the latter.  tx_pend_num/tx_sent_num play the roles of the
vendor's tx_list_num/sending_flag.  The flush runs on the work thread:
the completion callback holds only the spinlock and cannot take the mutex.
Frames still queued have never been handed to the CP and carry no DMA
exposure, so a reset or ifdown may free them; frames already submitted
stay quarantined as before.

This does not fix the TTS stutter and is not offered as a fix for it.
Under that workload the batch size is always 1, because segments arrive
at roughly 1.4 per second and there is never a second frame waiting.  The
value is the dropped-frame path and the upload direction, where ASR
already sustains 33 KB/s and social mode is meant to push five images a
second.  Measured over 441 frames: no resynchronisation, no regression.


########## 0e2ae48 ##########
feat(bk7258): let the Wi-Fi driver hold a whole mailbox batch of frames

The CP may chain up to BK7258_WIFI_MAX_LIST frames into one mailbox
transaction.  wifi_handle_data() could only place four, because each queue
slot carried a 1514-byte copy of the frame, and it holds packet_lock and the
driver spinlock across the whole list so nothing drains mid-loop.  Frames past
the fourth were dropped in silence: the CP had already been told the list was
taken, nothing retried them, and no counter recorded it.

Queue netpkt pointers instead.  A slot is 8 bytes rather than 1520, so sixty
of them cost 480 bytes where four cost 6080, and g_wifi shrinks from 32640 to
27040.  wifi_locate_rx_frame() replaces wifi_copy_rx_frame(): it validates the
CP's descriptor and reports where the payload is, and the copy runs with the
spinlock dropped because netpkt_copyin() reaches iob_trycopyin(), which takes
further buffers when it needs them.  The reset generation is re-checked after
the copy, so a CP that restarts mid-copy costs one dropped frame rather than a
corrupt one.  wifi_receive() now only dequeues -- its netpkt_alloc() and
netpkt_copyin() were the second copy of every frame and are gone.

Emptying the queue used to mean zeroing three indices, which was free when a
slot was static storage.  A slot now owns a netpkt, so the four reset sites
take the pointers out under the lock and free them after dropping it, the way
wifi_tx_pending_drop_locked() already defers netpkt_free().

The RX quota stays separate from the slot count at 20.  It cannot be the slot
count: netdev_lower_register() rejects a device whose quotas exceed the buffer
pool, quota_is_valid() wanting quota[TX] + quota[RX] <= CONFIG_IOB_NBUFFERS,
and sixty against eight TX slots came to 68 over a pool of 40 -- registration
returned -EINVAL and the board came up with no wlan0 at all.

Also counts what the receive path throws away, which is how the above was
found.  A channel 2 list mixes arriving frames with our own transmitted
buffers coming back, so those are counted apart; rx_queue_full is a frame with
nowhere to go, rx_alloc_fail is one with no buffer, and the three silent
transmit refusals get counters too.  bk7258_net_get_counters() hands the lot
back as data rather than printing, because the console is one of the
transport's own channels and a readout that logged would add the traffic it
was trying to measure.  netbench reads them either side of a transfer.

Measured against a host on the same network, fifteen seconds each way:

  before  36.8 KB/s, 32 frames dropped for want of a slot, sender pinned at a
          congestion window of 1 with 52% of segments retransmitted
  after   67-119 KB/s, no drops at all, congestion window 7-12

Pacing the sender so that no transaction carried more than three frames had
already given 63.6 KB/s with nothing dropped and nothing retransmitted, which
is what pointed at the queue rather than the radio.  The remaining loss on
this link is outside the AP: a run with a healthy window, 23 buffers free and
zero driver drops still saw 39% retransmission.

This does not claim to fix the TTS stutter.  The defect and the improvement
are measured; the symptom has not been re-tested, because that needs someone
to speak to the device.

########## 4ca2746 JPEG perf ##########
perf(bk7258): take the hardware JPEG path from half the sensor rate to all of it

640x480 delivered 11.95-15.0 fps against a sensor that produces about 30.
The encoder was never the limit: every delivered frame paid a full
Huffman/MCU walk over the whole scan -- 2400 macroblocks at 640x480,
measured at ~35 ms, more than a frame period -- and frames arriving inside
that window were dropped.  Measured after this change: 24.36-29.18 fps at
640x480, 17.39-17.87 at 480x480, validator down to 1-4 ms.

Four changes, each with its own reason:

  - The sensor now has a stream enable.  GC2145's DVP output pads are
    register 0xF2, which the vendor's own table writes 0x00 to in its
    preamble and 0x0F to at the end of gc2145_init (dvp_gc2145.c) -- its
    init sequence is "pads off, configure, pads on".  This port had copied
    both writes into one table, so the pads opened at init() and never
    closed, and the capture module always enabled the encoder somewhere in
    the middle of a frame.  The framework already calls in the vendor's
    order (v4l2_cap.c runs IMGDATA_START_CAPTURE before
    IMGSENSOR_START_CAPTURE), so the only thing missing was a sensor that
    stays quiet in between.  bit_fixed, the count of frames needing a
    one-bit entropy repair, went from about a third of them to zero.

  - Recovery is funnelled through one flag.  Only the encoder's own
    frame_err could trigger the VSYNC-boundary reset; a frame lost to a
    missing EOI or an unrecognisable span left the hardware running with
    whatever phase had caused it.  The vendor keeps exactly one such flag
    (dvp_driver_handle_t::error) for this reason.

  - Entropy validation reads a prefix.  Bit alignment is a property of the
    whole scan -- a stream read one bit off desynchronises within a few
    blocks -- so 128 macroblocks settle it, while the whole frame is what
    made it expensive.  What a prefix cannot see is corruption past it, so
    the vendor's own check is added alongside: the bytes the DMA delivered
    against the hardware's byte_count_pfrm less the five CRC bytes it
    appends.  That comparison is recorded but not enforced
    (CONFIG_BK7258_CAMERA_JPEG_RECONCILE=n): measured, 480x480 matches
    exactly on every frame while 640x480 has a few frames out by up to
    25 KB, so the window has to be understood before it can reject.
    Rejection semantics are unchanged either way -- a frame that does not
    validate is still failed closed, never delivered.

  - The cost is now measurable.  CONFIG_ARCH_PERF_EVENTS gives the DWT
    cycle counter, which is the only clock on this core fine enough to see
    a 25 KB copy (CONFIG_USEC_PER_TICK is 1000).  stop_capture reports
    per-frame copy/header/scratch/realign cycles, the FIFO drain spin
    count, and the core clock the cycles imply -- 481-487 MHz measured
    against the 480 MHz CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ had only ever asserted.

Two things the measurements settled: the bounded wait for the encoder FIFO
to empty never spins at all (drain spins max=0), so the vendor is right not
to have one; and the delivery rate is now bound by whoever consumes the
frames rather than by this driver, which is why hw_busy is the flag saying
whether a frame-rate sample is meaningful.

Also corrects two comments that described the pre-2651af2 design: the drain
ring is stopped and re-armed at every EOF, and it is armed at a ring slot
rather than at the V4L2 buffer.

New knobs, all defaulting to the existing behaviour except the validation
prefix: BK7258_CAMERA_JPEG_VALIDATE_MCUS (128, 0 = whole frame),
BK7258_CAMERA_JPEG_RECONCILE (n), BK7258_CAMERA_JPEG_DRAIN_SPINS (100000),
BK7258_CAMERA_JPEG_DMA_DEST_BURST (0), BK7258_JPEG_BITRATE_PCT (100).

Verified on the board: 480x480 and 640x480 structurally valid with no =no
in any frame, ring_over/no_soi/short/hdr_fail all zero; 864x480 still falls
back to software and reports no hardware counters; UYVY preview 15.55 fps
with 0 errors.  Host side, app/web_tool/host/tests `make jpeg-header` is
18 checks 0 failures, including six new ones for the prefix mode and one
that pins the tradeoff it makes.


########## fc1eb90 ##########
perf(bk7258-ap): move 30 KB of JPEG lookup table into the network buffer pool

The IOB pool decides how fast a download can run, because
tcp_get_recvwindow() advertises iob_navail(true) * CONFIG_IOB_BUFSIZE.  A
measured fifteen-second download bottomed out at 9 free buffers of 40, which
is 1 once CONFIG_IOB_THROTTLE is subtracted, and the far end saw the window
collapse to 1094 bytes and spent 20% of the transfer waiting on it.  The pool
also cannot be moved to PSRAM: iob_initialize() runs before the CP powers
PSRAM up, so every buffer has to come out of SRAM.

SRAM was at 94.9%.  It pays for the extra buffers by giving up JPEG_FAST_BITS,
dropped from 12 to 8 so the four Huffman acceleration tables cost 2 KB instead
of 32 KB.  Nothing depends on a hit in those tables -- jpeg_decode_huff()
falls through to the canonical bit-at-a-time decoder whenever an entry is zero
-- eight bits is what libjpeg has used as HUFF_LOOKAHEAD for decades, and the
tables are only touched while realigning a captured camera frame, never on the
network path.  The trade is 30720 bytes of decode acceleration for 20 network
buffers.

Halving the throttle to 4 costs nothing and does the same job at the low water
mark, at the price of a smaller reserve for callers that allocate unthrottled.

Net effect on memory: 93.27% of RAM against 94.89% before, so the pool grew by
half while the image got smaller.  The build guard moves with the value, and
gains a second check on the throttle, because the reason the old guard gave for
pinning the pool at 40 -- eleven buffers for a 16 KiB TLS record -- is a floor
and not a ceiling.

Measured after the change, at the rate the link carries cleanly: 64.0 KB/s
offered and 64.0 KB/s delivered, no retransmissions, no drops, and 57 of the
60 buffers still free.  Above that rate the link itself starts losing frames
and no amount of buffering helps -- a paced 120 KB/s still lost 30% -- so this
removes the AP as the constraint rather than raising the ceiling.


</content>
</file>

fix(camera): stop the 480x480 capture after three frames, and un-throttle it

Two independent causes, both measured rather than reasoned about.

The frame-rate control was a pacer, and because the pipeline is demand-driven
the wait cannot overlap encoding: at 640x480, where one frame already takes
close to the interval, it cost a factor of 2.4 -- 3.01 fps down to 1.25.
Re-timing from encode completion was tried and measured worse (480x480: 4.39 ->
2.26 fps), so it was reverted; the reason is recorded in the code so it is not
tried again.

The other cause was thread priority. A consumer running below LPWORK (100) gets
starved by the encoder and the sender, never returns a buffer, and the
demand-driven driver then has nothing to fill -- the capture simply stopped
after three frames. The same code at the default priority never showed it.

The driver also gained split counters (busy / nobuf / due_in) so the next
occurrence says which of the three it is instead of just "it stopped".

+# TTS 卡顿排查：云端侧排除记录
+
+> 测量日期：2026-08-31　测量方式：主机侧对照实验（方案 1）
+> 结论：**云端服务无问题，故障在设备侧。** 同时查实两处客户端缺陷。
+
+## 1. 起因
+
+板上闲时语音助手播报时只发出少量破碎声音。设备日志（2026-08-31 20:53 一轮）：
+
+```
+[volc_tts_ws] TTS request: reqid=01cf094c-... text=267 bytes
+[volc_tts_ws] idle timeout: 6 chunk(s) 94208 byte(s) (2944 ms audio),
+              last seq 13 flags 1, 0 ping(s) 1 ack(s) 0 frontend 0 skipped
+vs_voice: tts synthesis returned 0 after 28765 ms
+vs_voice: playback starved 4 time(s)
+vs_audio: network buffers low-water 25 of 40
+vs_audio: playback watermark 1000 -> 2000 ms after 4 underrun(s)
+```
+
+267 字节 UTF-8 中文约 89 字，按正常语速应产出 18~22 秒音频，实收 2944 ms，约为应有量的 1/6。
+
+## 2. 对照实验设计
+
+在**同一网络出口**用主机复刻设备的请求，逐帧记录到达时刻。探针严格对齐 `packages/ai_agent/src/voice/volc_tts_ws.c`：
+
+| 项 | 值 |
+|---|---|
+| 端点 | `wss://openspeech.bytedance.com/api/v1/tts/ws_binary` |
+| 认证头 | `Authorization: Bearer;<token>`（分号、无空格） |
+| 火山帧头 | 8 字节 `0x11 0x10 0x10 0x00` + 4 字节大端长度 |
+| 请求体 | `app{appid,token,cluster}` / `user{uid:"agent"}` / `audio{voice_type, encoding:"pcm", rate:16000, speed_ratio:1.0}` / `request{reqid, text, text_type:"plain", operation:"submit"}` |
+| cluster | `volcano_tts` |
+| voice | `zh_female_meilinvyou_emo_v2_mars_bigtts` |
+| 文本 | 88 字 / 264 字节（与失败那轮的 267 字节对齐） |
+
+两处**故意与设备不同**，这是实验价值所在：
+
+1. 空闲预算放宽，并在设备的 10 秒处标记 `DEVICE WOULD HAVE DECLARED EOF HERE`，单独统计该点之后还到了多少音频——设备自己测不出这个数。
+2. 打印所有 `msg_type`。`volc_tts_ws.c` 只检查 `0xB0`/`0xC0`/`0xF0`，其它类型直接落到循环尾，不计入 `skipped`/`acks`/`frontend`，在板上不可见。
+
+主机侧环境：有线出口，到 `openspeech.bytedance.com` TLS 可达（约 565 ms，TLSv1.3，证书 CN `*.bytedance.com`）。凭据仅经环境变量传入，未落盘。
+
+## 3. 测量结果
+
+两次独立运行，结果一致：
+
+| | 板子 | 主机（第 1 次） | 主机（第 2 次） |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| chunk 数 | 6 | 41 | 38 |
+| 音频总量 | 2944 ms | **18358 ms** | **17851 ms** |
+| 到货窗口 | — | 0.53 → 2.68 s | 0.53 → 3.10 s |
+| 到货速率 | （见 §5 更正） | **约 8.5x 实时** | **约 5.7x 实时** |
+| 首帧延迟 | 未知 | 0.53 s | 0.53 s |
+| 帧间隔 | — | 均 69 ms / 最大 343 ms | 同量级 |
+| 结束方式 | `idle timeout`，无终止符 | 收到终止帧 | 收到终止帧 |
+
+**服务端毫无问题**：88 字文本产出约 18 秒音频，2~3 秒内全部送达，速率达实时的 5.7~8.5 倍。
+
+### 3.1 板子收到的是完整流的前缀
+
+对齐两侧帧序列，板子的 6 个 chunk 正好是主机最前面 6 帧：
+
+```
+448 + 512 + 512 + 448 + 512 + 512 = 2944 ms   ← 与板子 6 chunk / 94208 字节吻合
+```
+
+主机收完这 6 帧只用了 **0.79 秒**。也就是说板子前 2.9 秒音频接收完全正常，之后**一个字节都没再来**。
+
+### 3.2 板子那 10 秒是彻底静默，不是变慢
+
+- 主机实测服务端每 **5.000 秒**发一次 PING（`5.000 / 10.000 / 15.000 …`），板子 28 秒会话里 `0 ping(s)`
+- 板子报的是 `idle timeout` 而非 `-EPROTO`，说明 `tls_read_all()` 是在**干净的帧边界**上连续 20 次拿到 `-ETIMEDOUT`——客户端在正常询问，底层无数据
+
+结论：不是下发慢，是**收到约 94 KB 之后连接硬卡死**。
+
+## 4. 顺带查实的两个客户端缺陷
+
+### 4.1 终止帧被当作垃圾丢弃（会导致每次回复固定多等 10 秒）
+
+主机看到的真正结束帧：
+
+```
+t=3.115s   12 bytes   seq=-62   flags=3   （无 PCM 载荷）
+```
+
+12 字节 = `4 字节头 + 4 字节 seq + 4 字节 size`。而 `volc_tts_ws.c` 的判断顺序是：
+
+```c
+size_t audio_off = volc_hdr_len + 8;              /* = 12 */
+if (flen <= audio_off) { skipped++; continue; }   /* 12 <= 12 命中，丢弃 */
+...
+if (seq < 0) { ended = "final sequence"; break; } /* 永远执行不到 */
+```
+
+`flen <= audio_off` 先命中，负 seq 终止判据永不执行。**即使一次回复完整收完，设备也检测不到结束，必定走满 20×500 ms = 10 秒空闲预算。** 本次板上 `0 skipped` 是因为压根没收到这一帧。
+
+### 4.2 `sequence` 不是逐帧递增，此前的"丢帧"推断不成立
+
+主机实测序号：`5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 19, 21, …` 有跳号。因此板子"`last seq 13` 却只有 6 帧"属正常现象，**不存在丢帧**。
+
+## 5. 对此前两处错误结论的更正
+
+**更正一：不存在"云端下发速率 r≈0.16"。** 该数字是把被截断的 2944 ms 除以一段几乎全是死寂的墙钟时间（含 10 秒空闲预算）算出的假象。实测服务端速率为 5.7~8.5x 实时。此前引用的 `app/velasight/Kconfig` 注释里 "0.60x–1.93x"、"4 s 音频 / 5.5 s 墙钟"、"r=0.73" 等历史记录，均未能在本次测量中复现，不应作为设计依据。
+
+**更正二：`network buffers low-water 25 of 40` 不能用于排除设备侧。** `iob_min` 仅在 TTS 写回调内采样（`vs_audio.c:1790-1800`），卡死开始后不再有 chunk 到达、回调不再执行，因此那个 25 **只描述健康的头 2.9 秒，对卡死期间一无所知**。
+
+## 6. 修正后的因果链
+
+1. 板子正常收下前约 2.9 秒音频（约 94 KB）
+2. 连接卡死，音频与 PING 全断，10 秒无任何字节
+3. 客户端空闲预算耗尽判 EOF，丢弃 5/6 回复 → **"少量"**
+4. 已到的 2.9 秒因预缓冲闸门被墙钟提前放开而饿死 4 次 → **"破碎"**
+
+第 4 步的闸门缺陷（`vs_audio.c:1356-1362`，字节阈值 `prebuffer` 与墙钟阈值 `prebuffer_ms` 共用同一个 W 且取 OR，导致 r<1 时有效头量被打成 r 倍）独立存在且仍然成立，但相对第 2 步属次要问题。
+
+## 7. 待验证的主嫌（H2）
+
+设备日志显示 mbedtls 层拿到的是干净超时，问题在 mbedtls 之下：TCP/IP 栈、Wi-Fi 驱动或链路。
+
+量级上 IOB 池吻合：主机数据显示音频帧为 16384+12 字节的大帧、成组到达且组内间隔仅 13~15 ms。一个 16 KB TLS 记录约需 11 个 IOB，连续三帧在途约 48 KB ≈ 33 个 IOB，而 `CONFIG_IOB_NBUFFERS=40`、`CONFIG_IOB_THROTTLE=8` 使读缓存有效视角约 32 个——正好在临界点。一次突发打空池子 → 通告零窗口 → 若零窗口探测/恢复未走通即永久死锁，与"音频和 PING 全断且不恢复"的现象吻合。
+
+**此为假设，尚未验证。**
+
+## 8. 复现方式
+
+探针脚本当前位于 `/tmp/tts_probe.py`（标准库实现，主机上无 websocket 包）。运行：
+
+```bash
+VOLC_APPID='<app_id>' VOLC_TOKEN='<token>' python3 /tmp/tts_probe.py
+```
+
+可选覆盖：`VOLC_CLUSTER` `VOLC_VOICE` `VOLC_RATE` `TTS_TEXT` `TTS_IDLE_S`。
+
+注：本次测量所用凭据已在排查过程中以明文出现，建议轮换。
